rounds.title: Pane edge
rounds.note: The tooltip pane fills with --et-surface-background-solid of the surface it inherits, so on the base surface the fill equals the base (1.00:1 in both schemes) and only the 1 px border and the shadow mark the edge. In light the border (229 on 255) is 1.26:1 but the shadow carries the edge. In dark the border (64 on 23) is 1.73:1 and the shadow can only darken 23 to 21, so the pane and arrow edge nearly vanish. Text on fill passes: 12.63:1 light, 13.33:1 dark. Every variant leaves the light scheme pixel-identical and changes no background colour; the arrow edge follows the pane border.

a.note: Today's look: dark border --et-surface-border-solid 64, 1.73:1 against the base and the equal fill; light 229, 1.26:1 plus shadow.

b.note: Pick. Dark-only 1 px ring 77 = color-mix(--et-surface-color-solid 24 %, --et-surface-background-solid) on pane border and arrow: 2.12:1 against the base (today 1.73). The same --et-surface-ring-solid token as the foundations/elevation round, so tooltip and overlay panes share one dark edge; under the elevation round's own 2.61 because a tooltip mixes over the 23 base, not the 38 elevated fill.

c.note: Dark-only 1 px ring 102 = the same mix at 35 %: 3.1:1 against the base, the WCAG 1.4.11 line. Reads as a drawn outline next to the text, and departs from the 24 % elevation ring, so tooltips would get their own edge value.
